findings.title: Long overflow stimulus is separate from the bounded Windows sender
findings.evidence: send_uart_baud.py caps payload at64 bytes. The archived overflow check expects a prefilled1024-event FIFO.
findings.recommendation: Document the actual long-burst Windows stimulus separately; do not claim the archived notebook alone reproduces the overflow test.

driver_panel_review.configuration: Six supported rates; selected code read from hardware B0..B5 signature. Wrong/old overlay rejected.
driver_panel_review.switching: Requires unread FIFO count zero; exports read records before SET_BAUD; starts new session only after verified ACK/readback.
driver_panel_review.clear: Begins new record by saving already-read records first then clearing FIFO. Unread events are intentionally discarded, so documented stop/read/export order matters.
driver_panel_review.failure: Disk-save failure blocks clear/switch; uncertain hardware-command completion blocks retry; hardware error permits export of already-read records under original configuration.
driver_panel_review.read: One event committed at a time, at most256 per click; table200, session10000, hardwareFIFO1024; manual polling rather than continuous lossless streaming.
driver_panel_review.time: Metadata explicitly distinguishes host operation timestamps and calculated baud from measured waveform/FPGA timestamps.

dependencies.board_platform: Linux/PYNQ; fcntl lock is Unix-only; not a Windows notebook target.
dependencies.windows_sender: COM5 is an example/current adapter setting; selectable six baud,8N1,no flow control; bounded1..64-byte hex/ramp or requested20ms BREAK+100ms gap+55AA.
dependencies.offline_tests: stdlib unittest, mock MMIO and widgets; no FPGA/browser execution.
